gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much space you can actually use or what each usable terabyte costs in power: the Synology BeeStation Plus 8 TB gives 6.98 TB usable and draws 14.75 W while in use (2.11 W per usable TB, about 129 kWh a year if it is in use around the clock), and the BeeStation 4 TB gives 3.45 TB usable at 7.85 W (2.28 W per usable TB).
standout_why: ChatGPT's answer ran no searches, and its result list is empty, so it cites no rival pages. Its two catalog cards, the Synology DS224+ and the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus, are diskless NAS units. Its answer gives no usable capacity, no power draw and no per-TB figure. Our current page already has the 6.98 TB and 3.45 TB usable figures, so the new part is the derived watts per usable TB and the yearly energy.
decides: This confirms the BeeStation Plus 8 TB as the most usable storage per box and per watt among the units that come with drives: 6.98 TB at 2.11 W/TB, against 2.28 W/TB for the BeeStation 4 TB. Neither has a mirror. The Buffalo LS720D0802 holds two 4 TB drives, so mirrored in RAID 1 it keeps only 4 TB raw, half its label. Its default RAID mode could not be sourced, so the page should present that as a choice the buyer makes, not as a stated default. Prices could not be sourced, so cost per usable TB can't be ranked yet.

Yearly energy range
findings.note: Hibernating all year: 2.83 W × 8,760 h ÷ 1,000 = 24.8 kWh. In use all year: 14.75 W × 8,760 h ÷ 1,000 = 129.2 kWh.

Raw capacity if mirrored (RAID 1)
findings.note: Maker page: LS720D0802 = 8 TB in 2 bays, supports RAID 0/1/JBOD, ships with 'RAID already configured' (level not named). With two 4 TB drives mirrored: 8 TB ÷ 2 = 4 TB raw.

findings.label: Maximum power draw
findings.note: Maker gives only a maximum, so it can't be compared directly with Synology's in-use figure. Worst case per raw TB if mirrored: 48 W ÷ 4 TB = 12 W/TB.
